::: {.callout-note}
**Coming soon.** A short reminder that agentic coding accelerates the
mechanical parts of research and leaves the substantive parts exactly
where they were — with you.
:::

## The list

### Specification

What's the right model? What controls? What functional form? What sample
restriction? Claude can implement any of these; it cannot tell you which
is correct for your question.

### Identification

Why does this design recover a causal effect? What threats remain? What
robustness checks address them? The model can list textbook threats; it
cannot judge whether *your* setting has them.

### Interpretation

What does the coefficient mean? Is it economically large? Is it consistent
with prior estimates? What's the policy or theoretical takeaway? Claude
can produce confident-sounding interpretations that are wrong about your
context.

### Contribution

What's new here? Why should anyone care? Where does this sit in the
literature? Claude has read a lot but has no taste — it cannot tell you
whether your contribution is interesting.

### Authorship

Anything you submit goes out under your name. Claude is a tool — don't
list it as a co-author, don't pretend it didn't help, and disclose LLM
use as your journal requires.

### The hard problem

The model is good enough that you'll be tempted to outsource judgment
disguised as code: "write the empirical strategy section", "decide which
controls to include", "write the limitations section". Notice when you're
about to do this. The cost of bad judgment doesn't go down because the
typing got faster.

*This page is still an outline. If a fuller version would help your work,
email me and I'll prioritize it.*
